subject: Follow-up: connection pool & concurrency SLOs — action items
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Torres <jamie@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today — conn pool / concurrency targets & next steps

Hey Jamie — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into procurement: 

Summary of what you shared (please correct anything I got wrong):
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~1,200 connected clients during Black Friday simulation windows (15 minute bursts).
- Typical sustained concurrency outside peak: ~150 parallel sessions.
- Latency target: P95 generation latency <= 350ms for 512 token responses.
- Throughput need: roughly 35 requests/sec sustained during bursts, with spikes up to 120 req/sec for short windows.
- Streaming: client-side streaming of incremental tokens is required for the chat UI (WS + HTTP fallback).
- Connection behavior: clients maintain persistent HTTP/2 connections, reuse multiplexing; also expect bursts of new TCP connections from mobile clients.

Proposed Redwood follow-ups: 
1) Ben will sketch two quota profiles (Conservative / Aggressive) and a recommended connection-pooling config for your infra pattern. Expect a spreadsheet with token/QPS rows.
2) Rishi to comment on streaming setup and best practice for WS vs long-poll fallback (we discussed KV cache implications for streaming).
3) Jamie — can you attach the load-profile spreadsheet you referenced on the call (sample rows by minute) so we can validate our batching and prefilling recommendations? You mentioned an internal "conn_profile.xlsx".
4) I'll loop in engineering for a quick infra checklist (TLS session reuse, idle timeouts, NAT/ephemeral port considerations) ahead of a formal Dedicated capacity quote.

Attachments: acme_connpool_requirements.xlsx (placeholder you said you'd share).

Next steps: Ben to send quota options by end of day Thursday; Rishi to reply with streaming notes by EOD Friday. If that works I'll prepare a draft SOW/quote for review.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee

From: Jamie Torres <jamie@acmeretail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: SaaS Infra <infra@acmeretail.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — conn pool / concurrency targets & next steps

Thanks Soojin — that matches our notes closely. A couple clarifications: 

- The 1,200 "connected clients" are devices, but only ~60% will be actively sending/receiving during the 15-min peak windows (so effective concurrent requests ~= 720). We included the higher number to be conservative in capacity planning.
- P95 latency target is negotiable if you can guarantee lower tail for streaming token delivery (i.e., we care more about perceived typing latency than full-response latency). If streaming can consistently keep token gaps <= 40ms, we can accept slightly higher P95 for final payloads.
- For spikes: those 120 req/sec events are typically short (30–90s) and originate from external integrations (order engines) rather than the mobile clients. Those should probably be handled by an autoscaled Dedicated pool or a fallback regional hosted capacity.

I've attached the conn_profile.xlsx sample we referenced. Also attaching a short note from infra about NAT port exhaustion we've seen in our test labs — that will affect how we configure connection reuse.

On procurement: we'll need a formal quote + SLA options (bronze/silver/gold) and confirmation of rate-limit ceilings per API key. We can probably accept a 10% throttle for backpressure during peak if there's a guaranteed retry window and preserve client-side idempotency.

—Jamie
Jamie Torres
Sr. Platform Engineer, Acme Retail
jamie@acmeretail.com

Attachments: conn_profile.xlsx, nat_exhaustion_notes.txt

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Torres <jamie@acmeretail.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood quota proposals + conn-pool recommendations

Jamie — attaching the Conservative and Aggressive quota profiles (see attached spreadsheet). High level summary inline: 

Conservative profile (good for short-term proof-of-value):
- Reserved concurrency: 200 tokens-worker slots (safely supports ~80 sustained req/sec at your avg token sizes)
- Burst allowance: +60% burst credit bucket (refill window 1 hour)
- Per-key rate limit: 250 req/min (with 429 retry-after semantics)
- Streaming: enabled with recommended WS keepalive 30s, max idle timeout 120s

Aggressive profile (recommended for Black Friday prep):
- Reserved concurrency: 900 tokens-worker slots (target supports sustained ~300 req/sec plus bursts)
- Burst allowance: +120% burst credit bucket (refill window 30 min)
- Per-key rate limit: 1,000 req/min with soft-shed to regional hosted fallback at 1,200 req/min
- Streaming: dedicated pooled workers for streaming flows; token-sharding to reduce KV cache thrash

Connection pool notes:
- Prefer long-lived HTTP/2 connections with multiplexing; set client-side pooling to reuse 64 concurrent streams per connection where possible.
- Encourage clients to use Keep-Alive and reduce new TCP connect churn; idle-ttl of 90s on our side is standard but configurable.
- For mobile clients behind NAT, recommend ephemeral port staggering and backoff jitter to avoid simultaneous reconnect storms.

SLO proposal: P95 <= 350ms for 512 tokens on Aggressive profile; P95 <= 600ms on Conservative (with streaming providing perceived latency improvements). We can formalize these in an SLA appendix.

Next steps (per Soojin's note): 
- I'll produce a short one-page quote matrix (Bronze/Silver/Gold) and attach a draft SLA appendix.
- Rishi, please add any streaming implementation constraints or gotchas (WS vs HTTP chunked) so we can include that in the SOW.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0199

Attachments: redwood_sla_options.pdf, quota_profiles_conservative_aggressive.xlsx

From: Jamie Torres <jamie@acmeretail.com>

Cc: SaaS Infra <infra@acmeretail.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood quota proposals + conn-pool recommendations

Thanks Ben — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A couple quick items before we route to procurement: 

- Please include a line-item for a temporary extra-burst credit add-on (one-time invoice) for our 2-week Black Friday testing window. We'll likely need +200% for the load test and then scale back.
- Can you confirm the per-connection multiplexing recommendation works with HTTP/2 proxies in front of our mobile CDN? We have an intermediate proxy that terminates TLS and forwards to Redwood. If it collapses connections we need to adjust stream-per-connection expectations.
- Security ask: we will need confirmation that audit logs include per-request API key and latency metrics for at least 90 days. Also need SOC 2 evidence for Dedicated deployment (we'll attach the questionnaire to the HubSpot deal).

If you can get the formal quote matrix + SLA appendix and the temporary burst add-on pricing to me by Monday EOD, I'll put it in the procurement queue. Otherwise we'll miss this sprint.

I'll upload the final conn_profile.xlsx into the HubSpot deal now (link above).

Cheers — Jamie
